APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF OCTOBER 1, 2019

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:05 pm

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Jerry Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  Item 16.1 will be continued to the meeting of October 15, 2019.

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Velasco  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.7.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:06 pm.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:10 pm.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with
  respect to Items 4.1 through 4.7.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of October 1, 2019

  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Jane Myring – How did we go from $9.0M in the hole to $834 in the black? We talk
  about transparency around here I think we have some accountability and I think it has to
  be brought up in laments terms so we all understand how we went from $9.0M in the
  hole to $834 in the black. I think that it is a real mind-boggling thing and there is
  something wrong somewhere. With all the warehouses and I am so tired of looking at
  big buildings that have nothing how much tax revenue do we make off of all those
  warehouses out there? I haven’t heard anything about tax revenue from them.

  Howard Owens – The main thing that brought me here was that you were negotiating
  the the purchase of property at 12159 Cherrylee. Question is, is this for a park? I have
  always told the equestrian unit it would be nice if the City would buy that and put in
  stables for the horses and we could have a substation in north part of El Monte. I don’t
  really think a park is perfect for there we have a dead end street, we have problems with
  transients, we have problems with graffiti. If we had a substation there maybe it would
  be okay because we would have someone watch over as we know now in our parks we
  don’t have that many employees that are at the parks to look over what is happening. I
  think you should talk to the neighbors behind and next to it to make sure they are willing
  to have people jump over their walls and stuff. My wife and daughter were taking a walk
  on Sunday and the observed a man dumping stuff on Cogswell near Cherrylee. Street
  lights are good in some ways but they don’t light up properly. The Christmas tree we are
  going to buy a $34,000 Christmas tree who is going to take care of it, where will it be
  stored, how much overtime.

  Anne Emmons – I am interested in the piece of property at 12159 Cherrylee. I was here
  about 16 months ago proposing that there was this two acre parcel there and why
  couldn’t this land be bought by the City we really need a Police substation. I know
  currently the horses mounted units the horses are kept in Norco and that is really far
  away. If they really needed the horses to come out here for something that is going to
  take hours. I don’t think a park is a great idea I think it would draw the wrong kind of
  people.

  Mike Gomez – Just a very quick note. I want to first of all of you for having made the
  decision of making Alma Martinez your City Manager. I hadn’t had a chance to make
  that public comment but I really wanted to congratulate the City Council for doing that.
  Alma has been an incredible Assistant City Manager and has done a tremendous job. I
  think you guys have made a wonderful decision and having done that you have done a
  lot of firsts. This is the first time that a woman has been the City Manager of a major
  City especially in the San Gabriel Valley. I want to congratulate you and want to publicly
  welcome Ms. Martinez.

  Gabriel Ramirez – I know that the City Council shall be under no obligation to respond to
  or deliberate upon any specific questions or comments posed by speaker or take any
  action on any issues raised by speaker. Congratulations to the City Manager.

  Robert Law – There is a real problem in town regarding to property maintenance. On
  the corner of Lambert there is a home it is a Maxson home and it is in deplorable
  condition the weeds have grown up to the height of this stand. The other thing that I am
  concerned on is that on Lambert and Durfee there are needs to have a stop sign there.

14.  REGULAR AGENDA:
  14.1  Consideration and Approval of a City of El Monte Letter of Intent to Los Angeles
  County to Jointly Evaluate and Study the Potential Reuse of a Portion of the
  Maclaren Hall Site, Located at 4024 Durfee Avenue, El Monte, for Public Park
  Purposes and to Authorize the Appropriation of Three Million Dollars
  ($3,000,000) under the El Monte CIP No. 024 for the Prospective Development
  and Construction of such New Park.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Receive presentation from staff; and
  2. Consider and approve, by majority vote, the text of the proposed Letter of
  Intent and authorize the Mayor’s execution thereof.

  Total Cost: $3,000,000  Account No: EB-5 Fund 500
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  David Diaz – I am here to express my support for this item. The partnership
  between the City of El Monte and L.A. County to dedicate a portion of McClaren
  Hall for open space is paramount. We all know and it has been researched
  intensely by L.A. County and the Park Assessment we have approximately .41
  acres for 1,000 residents in the City of El Monte. I want to express my support
  for the project and as a resident and as an Executive Director for Active San
  Gabriel Valley we look forward to see this roll out and the partnership to continue
  so that families and children have places where they can belong and play and
  get to experience.

  Dr. Edward Zuniga – I am here to speak also in support of the City’s partnership
  with L.A. County and transforming what we see a wall into open space particular
  park space. I know that the District had been part of the Community Advisory
  Committee for this project. We are so excited to see what this project will bring.
  As part of this open space project we are addressing a population, a community
  which is one of the most vulnerable our students within that neighborhood don’t
  have much park space it is very dense. On behalf of our Board I want to make
  sure that we go on record that we are in support of open space and providing the
  necessities that our students need. We don’t have a legal soccer field for our
  community so imagine again what you can bring to our population.

  Diego Rodriguez – I am the COO of ALMA Family Center and I am also a
  licensed mental health provider. I am support of this project.

  m) Mayor Quintero
